title: Staying at Mrs. Martin's; Ralph Scull and Ink Williams show her Chicago
summary: She boarded with a religious family on Eberhart; Scull and Ink Williams took her sightseeing and said Jelly educated himself.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, Martin's. That's where I stayed with Mr. Martin's. Yeah, they were religious people, lovely people. And it was so nice because they were harvesting somewhere out in— out from Chicago, a lot of corn and stuff. They were canned and all that stuff. But I had never seen anybody canned anything in my life before. And I was so interested in it that I— every time I talked to him, I would talk about the things that we were doing during the day. He said, well, I'm content for you to see Chicago. But I didn't know anybody seen Chicago. It didn't matter with me whether I saw it or not. Because I wanted to see him and his friends and that for the end of it. But a Mr. Ralph Skull came and took me out one time. I understand now he's a teacher. He was in the University of Chicago. What's the name again? Ralph Skull. He's a plural player.

S—no, S-C-U-L-L. Oh, S-C-U-L-L. Skull. Skull. Yeah. He said S-K-U-L. Yes. S-T-U-L-L. But he's a plural player. And at the time, Ink Williams was pro— Oh, yes, I know him. Very popular. And Ink Williams, he sent Ink to take me out one day and tried to show me all the interesting places in Chicago to museums and things like that. Yes. And show me the different schools and the colleges. And he said how my brother had pulled up on his boots. He said, your brother really educated himself by pulling up on his bootstraps. He must have done a lot of work with me. Oh, he did a whole lot of work.
